# dtcloud_image (Data Source)

Looks up one image, by id or by name.

Use it to reference an image Terraform did not upload: one from the platform's own catalogue, or one
somebody built by hand. Declaring such an image as a resource would hand Terraform ownership of it,
and a later destroy would delete it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# By name. The lookup refuses an ambiguous answer rather than picking the first
# match, because image names are not unique on the platform.
data "dtcloud_image" "ubuntu" {
  name = "Ubuntu 22.04"
}

data "dtcloud_image" "by_id" {
  id = var.image_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) ID of the image to look up. Give this or `name`.
- `name` (String) Name of the image to look up. Give this or `id`. It is an error for more than one image to carry the name.

### Read-Only

- `min_disk` (Number) Smallest volume, in GB, a machine built from this image needs. `0` when the platform reports none.
- `os_distro` (String) Distribution the image carries.
- `os_type` (String) `linux` or `windows`, when the platform reports it. Frequently empty here: the details endpoint passes the value straight through, while the list endpoint behind `dtcloud_images` guesses it from `os_distro` when it is missing.
- `size` (String) Size of the captured data, as the platform formats it — `1.2 GB` or `250 MB`. There is no endpoint that reports it as a number. An image with no data yet reads as `0 MB`.
- `status` (String) Status reported by the platform. `active` is the only status a machine can be built from; `queued` and `saving` mean the data is not there yet, and `killed` means the capture failed.
- `type` (String) How the platform categorises the image: `ISO` or `Template (VM)`. This is not `disk_format` — it is derived from it, and the two are not interchangeable.
- `uefi` (Boolean) Whether the image boots with UEFI firmware rather than BIOS.
- `visibility` (String) Who can see the image: `public`, `private`, `shared` or `community`.

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **A name must match exactly one image.** Image names are not unique on the platform. A lookup that
  matches several fails and lists the matching ids, rather than building machines from an image
  nobody chose.
* **Both lookups end on the details endpoint**, so the same fields come back however the image was
  found. That endpoint often reports an empty `os_type`; `dtcloud_images` fills it in from
  `os_distro`.
* **An image that does not exist is an error**, not an empty result.
